answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it can earn reputation or place high-value orders. The protocol caps influence by locked stake, so creating a thousand names does not multiply voting power unless the attacker also supplies a thousand times the capital. Sybils can still be created, but coordinated fraud risks forfeiting the bond when challenged and proven; the cost is tied to exposure time and capital, not merely computation. An ocean of cheap accounts cannot fake a pulse of trust, or turn a sonnet of claims into collateral.
